## Fixes

- **No more "Sign-in didn't finish" flash.** After signing in, returning to Obsidian could briefly show an error screen before the success one. Two completion paths (the return link and the automatic background check) were racing each other; now exactly one finishes the sign-in and only one screen appears.

No action needed — update via Community Plugins as usual.

## Fixes

- **Mobile sign-in opens the browser reliably.** On iOS the sign-in page sometimes never opened ("Waiting for the browser…" forever). External links now open through the platform's native link handling, which works consistently on iOS, Android, and desktop.
- **Sign-in finishes automatically — no callback required.** SystemSculpt now confirms your sign-in directly with systemsculpt.com while the browser is open, so you're signed in the moment you finish — even if the return link back into Obsidian is blocked or never fires. If the return link does arrive late, you're greeted as signed in instead of seeing an expired-request error.
- The sign-in screen now explains it completes automatically, and adds an "Open the sign-in page again" link in case the browser tab was lost. The paste-a-code fallback remains available.

No action needed — update via Community Plugins as usual.

## Guided plan gating, sign-in, and mobile purchase flow

- Sign in with a free account and stay signed in — paid features now open a guided plan modal (lifetime, monthly, compare plans, license re-sync) instead of failing silently
- One-time welcome for new users, plus a sign-in reminder in fresh chats
- Browser sign-in handoff with a manual connection-code fallback for devices where the deep link can't return
- Clear plan-required states across chat, transcription, audio processing, document conversion, Similar Notes, and Studio AI
- Mobile: modals are now full sheets with full-width touch-friendly actions

# SystemSculpt 6.6.4

SystemSculpt 6.6.4 makes Chat activity easier to scan and explore.

- Reasoning and adjacent tool calls now appear in one compact activity drawer.
- Completed work uses clear labels such as `Reasoned`, `Read 4 files`, and `Searched 7 patterns`.
- Active work uses progress labels such as `Reasoning...` and `Reading 3 files...`.
- Each activity remains available inside the drawer with consistent icons, spacing, and ownership lines.

# SystemSculpt 6.6.3

SystemSculpt 6.6.3 makes new plugin releases clear, inviting, and easy to install.

- Each new version now gets one polished update modal across desktop and mobile.
- The “Let's evolve” action opens the official SystemSculpt page in Obsidian Community Plugins.
- Dismissing the modal keeps the persistent desktop status-bar reminder without showing the modal again for that version.
- The manual `Check for updates` command can reopen the modal at any time.
- Obsidian Community Plugins remains the only owner of download, installation, activation, and rollback.

# SystemSculpt 6.6.2

SystemSculpt 6.6.2 makes new releases visible inside Obsidian within about one minute.

- SystemSculpt checks for a published release at startup, every minute, and when the user returns to Obsidian.
- Each release gets one notice per app session, plus a persistent desktop status-bar action until installation.
- A manual `Check for updates` command gives explicit current, available, or unavailable feedback.
- Update checks use first-party static release metadata and never call the GitHub Releases API at runtime.
- Obsidian Community Plugins remains the only owner of download, installation, activation, and rollback.

# SystemSculpt 6.6.1

SystemSculpt 6.6.1 makes ChatView failures recoverable and easier to diagnose without exposing chat content.

- Partial assistant output now stays visible when a response fails.
- Failed responses show compact Retry and Copy report actions without an empty assistant row.
- Retry can recover in the same chat without leaving stale active content or locking the composer.
- Client incident reports now include bounded rendering, scroll, resource, transport, lifecycle, and failure evidence.
- Incident reports use canonical JSON, stay vault-local, and exclude prompts, responses, paths, tool payloads, conversation IDs, request IDs, and attachments.
- Copied report bytes remain exact after plugin reload, including storage-failure memory fallback.
- Failed response drawers stay closed, terminal animations stop, and scroll position stays stable.

# SystemSculpt 6.6.0

SystemSculpt 6.6.0 makes ChatView activity calmer, clearer, and more stable during long responses.

- Reasoning and tool calls now share one compact activity timeline.
- Active responses show a live `Working for` timer.
- Completed responses group activity inside one closed `Worked for` drawer.
- Earlier activity stays inside a closed `+N previous tool calls` drawer, with closed reasoning and tool detail drawers inside it.
- Final answers and Sources stay visible outside the activity drawer.
- Tool rows use compact status marks and clearer details without passive response tooltips.
- Streaming Markdown keeps stable rendered nodes, focus, selection, and interactive Obsidian content.
- Scroll anchoring keeps the current reading position stable as messages stream, drawers change, and embedded content loads.
- Cancelled responses keep one stable `You stopped after` presentation across live settlement and reload.

## 6.5.0

Live streaming release: assistant responses now stream token-by-token with near-provider latency. The plugin opts into the server's new live-delta event plane and paints the first token of every burst immediately, while the durable snapshot stream remains the sole execution authority — deltas are render hints only, and the transcript always heals from snapshots. Warm follow-up turns also drop two round trips (session resync and empty-context staging), and access refresh moved off the critical path.

Client pipeline cost per streamed token dropped from 11µs to 4µs, and end-of-turn perceived completion no longer waits on server settlement work.

# SystemSculpt 6.3.1

SystemSculpt 6.3.1 improves ChatView reliability and strengthens release testing.

- ChatView now gives clear guidance when a model safety filter stops a response.
- Live tests verify exact text, attachment, approval, and vault-write results.
- Tests select the active ChatView across split panes and pop-out windows.
- Release evidence now records the exact loaded plugin build and response timing.
- ChatView tests cover mobile use, long tool runs, replay safety, and failure recovery.

# SystemSculpt 6.3.0

SystemSculpt 6.3.0 moves managed chat to a server-owned streaming session and
makes web research activity clear in the conversation.

- Chat sessions now stream through the first-party SystemSculpt service while
  Obsidian remains the approval and vault-tool surface.
- Reconnects, queued turns, cancellation, approvals, and tool-result delivery
  remain recoverable across reloads and interrupted connections.
- Adjacent web searches appear in compact `Search the web (N)` groups.
- Expanded search groups show every approved query in its original order.
- Saved chats restore web-search groups without losing query details.
- Failed server searches are labeled as web-search failures, not vault errors.
- Release checks cover the production API target, thin-client boundaries,
  replay safety, mobile behavior, and supported Node and desktop platforms.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.7

SystemSculpt 6.2.7 makes managed chat follow-ups reliable after web search,
including chats first saved by older plugin builds.

- Reloaded chats no longer resend server-owned web-search history in a form the
  service rejects.
- A failed server-side search preserves its fallback response and no longer
  corrupts the next turn.
- Malformed or partially saved chat history now fails safely instead of
  inventing missing tool data.
- Editing an earlier message keeps vault-change confirmation safeguards even
  when saved tool metadata is malformed or reuses an identifier.
- Billing actions now accept only verified HTTPS SystemSculpt destinations.
- Local and hosted release gates now cover legacy reloads, request replay,
  streaming fragmentation, session fencing, mutation testing, Windows and
  macOS behavior, and supported Node versions.
- CI failure evidence is bound to the exact built plugin files, and mutation
  testing rejects targets that escape its isolated mirror.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.6

SystemSculpt 6.2.6 fixes follow-up messages in chats that used server-side web search.

- Continuing a chat after a web-search turn no longer fails with "SystemSculpt rejected this request." The search call's record stays in your local history, but it is no longer sent in a form the service must reject.
- Mixed batches of server-run and vault tools keep sending back only the vault results.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.5

SystemSculpt 6.2.5 fixes chat turns that use server-side web search.

- A chat turn whose only tools ran on the server (such as web search) now completes normally instead of failing with "This chat history could not be prepared safely."
- Mixed batches of server-run and vault tools continue to send back only the vault results.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.4

SystemSculpt 6.2.4 hardens Studio project persistence and managed image runs after three production incidents.

- Studio always opens project files it persisted, including managed image placeholders and files saved by other plugin versions; run readiness is still enforced when a graph actually runs.
- Entry points are treated as derived data: stale or version-skewed entry IDs no longer make a project unopenable, and OS junk files such as .DS_Store never invalidate project history.
- Failed managed image runs now report the service's specific failure reason instead of a generic "Managed job failed.", and transient polling errors are retried with backoff instead of failing the run.
- Text nodes connect to downstream text inputs, Chat renders server-executed tools, and the Audio Processor and managed agent surfaces are polished.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.3

SystemSculpt 6.2.3 keeps Studio image generation aligned with the current managed image service.

- Studio image nodes now expose only controls the managed service applies: Prompt, Image Count, and Aspect Ratio.
- Retired Seed and Image Size values are removed from existing Studio image nodes automatically.
- Image generation continues to use the latest managed engine without exposing provider configuration in the plugin.
- Streamed image downloads retain the strict file type, size, and integrity validation introduced in 6.2.2.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.2

SystemSculpt 6.2.2 makes Audio Processor easier to find and lets you choose the note you want before processing begins.

- Open Audio Processor directly from the Obsidian ribbon. The icon uses Obsidian's native ribbon behavior, so you can reorder or hide it with your other ribbon actions.
- Choose Detailed note + transcript, Meeting brief, or Clean transcript. Your preferred default is remembered for both audio files and YouTube links.
- Meeting brief focuses on outcomes, decisions, action items, and open questions. Clean transcript produces readable paragraphs without a separate summary.
- Chat responses now keep one stable visual shell from the first streamed update through completed history, with calmer reasoning and activity presentation and no lingering "Continuing" state.
- Consecutive actions of the same kind are grouped into plain-language summaries such as "Read 3 files," while failures and approval boundaries remain visible.
- Response copying now uses a compact icon with accessible success or failure feedback that does not move the layout.
- Edit a previous message directly in the transcript and resubmit from that point. SystemSculpt explains when later messages will be replaced and preserves your bottom-composer draft.
- SystemSculpt can use web search and other server-executed tools when they materially improve an answer, with ordered in-chat activity updates that remain compatible with older plugin clients.
- Selected PNG, JPEG, and WebP vault images are sent as real visual context. Unsupported, damaged, or oversized images now show a clear notice instead of disappearing silently.
- Studio image generations now download and save reliably when delivery uses streamed transfer, while retaining file type, size, and integrity checks.
- Temporary processing outages now show a friendly, retryable message instead of a raw service error.
- Pull request checks now validate the compiled mobile plugin bundle plus narrow-pane, touch, keyboard, and accessibility-sensitive chat behavior in a fast deterministic Node 22 pipeline.
- Automatic spoken-language detection, code-switching, YouTube processing, durable recovery, and linked transcript delivery remain available across every output choice.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.1

SystemSculpt 6.2.1 fixes Audio Processor uploads on Obsidian desktop. The plugin now lets the host set the binary request length, avoiding a restricted-header failure that could stop vault and device audio before it reached the SystemSculpt service.

- Vault and device audio can upload through Audio Processor on desktop without the `net::ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` failure.
- Signed binary uploads validate their expected byte length before sending while leaving the host-owned request header to Obsidian.
- The same transport safeguard covers Audio Processor, audio transcription, document processing, and image input uploads.
- YouTube processing, multilingual transcription, speaker-aware summaries, durable recovery, and credit settlement continue to use the server-owned 6.2 pipeline.

# SystemSculpt 6.2.0

SystemSculpt 6.2.0 brings a new Audio Processor to your vault. Choose existing audio or paste a YouTube link, then let SystemSculpt create a structured audio note and a linked, timestamped transcript without asking you to configure prompts or summary settings.

- Audio Processor accepts vault and device audio as well as public YouTube videos. Uploads continue on the SystemSculpt service, so long recordings do not need to keep Obsidian busy.
- Completed notes include source attribution, a concise summary, key points, decisions, action items, discussion topics, risks, blockers, and open questions when the source supports them. Empty sections are left out instead of filled with guesses.
- Multilingual transcription and speaker-aware audio processing are handled automatically. YouTube citations link back to the matching timestamp.
- Interrupted work can be resumed safely, and the transcript remains recoverable even if a later summary step cannot finish.
- Chat and Studio now use the current SystemSculpt AI model configuration while preserving the existing OpenRouter and vault-tool architecture.
- The unused legacy Workflow Automations settings, commands, and backlog screens are gone. Inbox audio transcription and Studio workflows remain available.
- Audio selection, recording recovery, local note delivery, and mobile behavior have additional safeguards for stale files, interrupted sessions, and duplicate completion attempts.

# SystemSculpt 6.1.0

SystemSculpt 6.1.0 makes the plugin materially safer on mobile and turns Studio projects into stable, agent-editable vault files instead of fragile private state.

- Settings, Chat, Similar Notes, Studio, modals, and fixed surfaces now share one adaptive mobile contract with safer host-capability checks, owned mobile chrome handling, better spacing, and portable fallbacks instead of desktop-only dead ends.
- `Copy Current File Path` now ships with `Mod+Shift+C`, prefers the actually focused vault-backed surface, and falls back to a vault-relative path on mobile hosts where absolute filesystem paths do not exist.
- `.systemsculpt` files are now the single editable Studio project source of truth. Generic vault file tools can edit them directly, while private Studio persistence paths remain guarded.
- Studio now validates agent-written project documents before write, keeps stable generated fields protected, and rejects malformed or unsafe project mutations before they hit disk.
- Project sessions are more resilient under autosave, reload, rename, and external-edit races. When a file edit beats an in-memory canvas save, Studio preserves the losing canvas as recovery/Undo instead of silently dropping work or overwriting the file.
- Studio image and media editing is less brittle: the inline image toolbar lives with the image surface, crop removal/deselection is explicit, and history/file-edit synchronization is better covered by tests.

# SystemSculpt 6.0.2

SystemSculpt 6.0.2 hardens license validation and makes future releases visible inside Obsidian.

- A temporary or malformed validation response can no longer be mistaken for an invalid paid license.
- Only an exact server rejection can clear a previously valid license. Connection failures preserve the last known state and show a retryable availability message.
- First-time activation retains the entered key during a temporary outage, so Retry remains available.
- New releases are announced in Obsidian, remain visible in the status bar until installed, and open the official Community Plugins page for installation.
- A manual `Check for updates` command and post-update confirmation make the installed state explicit.

Fixes Studio text-node editing so clicks place the caret where expected, including multiline Markdown, tables, code, and lists. Preview and edit layouts now stay aligned, including with Vim and relative line numbers enabled.

# SystemSculpt 6.0.0

SystemSculpt 6 replaces the old client-owned provider stack with one managed, cross-device architecture.

- Chat, transcription, embeddings, and Studio use SystemSculpt services with no provider-key setup.
- Chat is rebuilt from the ground up as a native agent workspace with streaming tool progress, inline approvals, durable artifacts, retries, cancellation, and queued follow-ups.
- Provider catalogs, model selection, local Pi execution, custom endpoints, and third-party tool-server configuration were removed.
- Existing managed chats continue normally. Chats tied to retired Pi or external-provider metadata open read-only.
- Settings migration removes retired credentials while preserving the SystemSculpt license, vault folders, Chat favorites, Studio projects, recorder preferences, embeddings, and workflows.
- The plugin supports desktop and mobile; local CLI, FFmpeg, and external-file Studio operations remain desktop-only.

# SystemSculpt 5.11.0

## What's New

SystemSculpt 5.11.0 makes Studio text nodes feel native to Obsidian and restores Chat Resend for desktop users. Text nodes now use Obsidian's Markdown editor, including live-preview formatting and task controls, while preserving the caret and edit history through Studio graph updates.

## Highlights

### Studio text editing

- **Native Markdown editing.** Studio text nodes now use Obsidian's embedded Markdown surface instead of a plain textarea, so headings, emphasis, code, links, lists, and task checkboxes behave like they do in a note.
- **Stable focus through graph updates.** Pointer placement, selection, scroll position, and focus survive the rerenders that happen while working in a Studio project.
- **Reliable save and history behavior.** Leaving a text node flushes the latest edit, a continuous editing session is grouped into one undo step, and deleting an empty node remains undoable and redoable.
- **Safer editor teardown.** Studio releases Obsidian's editor, focus, and keymap ownership even when a final commit or snapshot fails.

### Chat

- **Resend works again on desktop.** Resending from an earlier message no longer fails with `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: node:fs`. Desktop filesystem access now stays behind the plugin's desktop-only boundary, with a built-bundle regression check to prevent the failure from returning.

## Upgrade Notes

- No manual action is required.
- Minimum supported Obsidian version remains `1.4.0`.

## Verification

The release passed the plugin checks, full unit suite, built-bundle integration suite, and the Linux, macOS, and Windows GitHub end-to-end lanes. Native Studio editing and Chat Resend were also verified in the packaged plugin inside Obsidian.

# SystemSculpt 5.10.0

## What's New

SystemSculpt 5.10.0 is a focused security, privacy, and reliability release. It came out of a deep audit of the plugin and closes a cluster of correctness gaps: a secret no longer reaches a debug log, a syncable policy can no longer smuggle a blanket command-approval wildcard, rate limits now degrade gracefully, semantic search can no longer silently misalign, and settings failures are no longer swallowed. Every change shipped failing-test-first with a permanent CI guard, so the behaviors stay fixed.

## Highlights

### Security & privacy

- **License key kept out of logs.** The chat debug request log previously captured the full request headers, including your SystemSculpt license key. The debug payload is now redacted; the real request is unchanged.
- **No blanket command approval via sync.** A Studio agent policy can no longer carry a bare `*` wildcard that would auto-approve every CLI command. The wildcard is stripped when policies are parsed, ignored by the approval gate, and scrubbed from any policy already on disk.
- **License validity downgrades only on an authoritative rejection.** A real `401`/`403` from the license service now correctly marks the license invalid, while transient/network errors preserve your last-known-good state instead of locking you out on a blip.

### Reliability

- **Rate limits degrade gracefully.** The client now honors the server's `Retry-After` on a managed `429`, classifies bring-your-own-key `429`s as transient, and performs a bounded, abort-aware retry — with a guarantee that already-streamed content can never be replayed. This is the client complement to the server-side OpenRouter hardening.
- **Streams stop when a chat view closes.** Closing a chat now aborts its in-flight request instead of leaving the network stream, token spend, and render loop running in the background.
- **Honest edit-tool results.** The filesystem agent's edit tool now reports zero or partial edits accurately instead of claiming success when nothing (or only some) of the requested changes applied, and it skips no-op writes.
- **Settings failures are surfaced.** If saving (or backing up) settings fails — disk full, permissions, a sync lock — the error is now logged and shown once via a de-duplicated notice, instead of being silently swallowed and lost on reload.

### Semantic search

- **Embedding vectors stay aligned with their chunks.** Whitespace-only or empty inputs no longer shift the returned vectors out of alignment with their source chunks, which could silently corrupt semantic-search results. The provider now returns one slot per input and asserts the counts match.

### Developer experience

- **The CSS linter is now actually enforced.** The Obsidian-override hygiene linter that ships with the repo is wired into the check gate (locally and in CI), with a guard test proving it fails on an unscoped selector — so the rule it was written to catch is finally guaranteed.
- Removed a dead token-counter code path (and its orphaned support files) that referenced a dependency that was never installed.

## Upgrade Notes

- No manual action is required; settings migrate automatically on update.
- Minimum supported Obsidian version remains `1.4.0`.

## Verification

Every change in this release landed through its own pull request with the full CI matrix green — the unit suite and built-bundle integration suite, plus the macOS and Windows end-to-end lanes — and an automated review pass. Each fix added or tightened a permanent test guard at the cheapest layer that catches the regression. The release additionally ran the native release matrix: macOS desktop baselines, the Windows clean-install and desktop-baselines GitHub end-to-end check for the released commit, and the Android sync and runtime smoke lanes.

# SystemSculpt 5.9.0

## What's New

SystemSculpt 5.9.0 is a large feature and reliability release. It expands bring-your-own-key support to Claude and Gemini through their native APIs, makes BYOK users first-class (no license wall in chat), hardens startup and updates on every platform, and overhauls the embeddings and audio-transcription pipelines. It also lands the clearer license-renewal experience and a batch of chat and agent-mode improvements.

## Highlights

### Providers (bring your own key)

- **Claude (Anthropic) BYOK** via the native Messages API — add your Anthropic key and use Claude models directly in Chat.
- **Gemini (Google) BYOK** via the native `generateContent` API.
- A connected provider's models can no longer silently disappear from the Chat picker: a model-catalog status state machine keeps the dropdown honest.
- **BYOK users never hit a license wall.** When you run on your own provider key, chat no longer demands a SystemSculpt license, and a provider-key auth failure is reported as a provider problem ("Open Providers") rather than a subscription/renewal prompt.

### Platform reliability

- More reliable startup on Android and Linux, including a Node-free mobile bundle-load path so the plugin initializes without desktop-only APIs.
- A disabled plugin is now fully inert — no timers, listeners, or background work linger after you turn it off.
- Versioned settings migration with update safety: settings are migrated forward deterministically, with safe-mode and minimum-version fail-soft so a bad load can't wedge the plugin.

### Embeddings

- A portable embeddings index that survives Obsidian Sync and vault restore — export/import, snapshots, and automatic restore.
- Typed provider errors and more robust response parsing.
- Automatic retry with backoff for transient provider errors and rate limits.
- A bulk rebuild that can resume after an interruption even when auto-processing is off.

### Recording & transcription

- A typed transcription provider core: typed errors, a response normalizer, and an HTTP classifier shared across providers.
- **Self-hosted Whisper** support with config-time validation and a settings UI.
- A separate, configurable post-processing model for cleaning up transcripts.
- Captured audio is saved when iOS interrupts a recording (lock screen / phone call), so meetings aren't lost.
- Mobile recording bitrate is capped so long meetings stay within transcription limits.
- One-tap stop for the recorder — the stop control no longer needs repeat taps.
- YouTube transcription now returns an actionable message when the transcript service is over quota, instead of leaking a raw error.

### Chat & agent mode

- Agent mode is scoped to the individual chat instead of a global setting.
- The local Pi agent loop stops cleanly on repeated identical failing tool calls and surfaces an actionable error when a tool-use turn stalls.
- Favorite models are restored in the composer model picker.
- Filesystem agent tools run on mobile, and Folder Notes paths resolve correctly across all file tools.
- A per-chat toggle to hide system and tool messages.
- "Attach Context File" is available from the slash palette.

### License experience

- A clear, actionable renewal flow for expired or invalid SystemSculpt licenses, replacing the old generic stream error — with distinct copy and actions for expired vs. invalid vs. provider-key states.

## Upgrade Notes

- No manual action is required; settings migrate automatically on update.
- Minimum supported Obsidian version remains `1.4.0`.
- BYOK users: if you previously saw a license prompt while using your own provider key, that no longer happens — chat runs on your key.

## Verification

Plugin checks, the full unit suite, and the built-bundle integration suite passed locally. The release also ran the native release matrix: macOS desktop baselines, the Windows clean-install and desktop-baselines GitHub end-to-end check for the released commit, and the Android sync and runtime smoke lanes. Every change in this release landed through CI with the macOS and Windows E2E lanes green on its pull request.

# SystemSculpt 5.8.1

## What's New

SystemSculpt 5.8.1 is an OpenAI provider setup patch. Adding an OpenAI API key now makes GPT-5.4 Mini available in the Chat model picker, and chat requests for it route to OpenAI using your key.

This continues the provider setup work from 5.7.1, which fixed the same kind of "provider connected but its model is missing from Chat" gap for xAI.

## Highlights

- A connected OpenAI provider now adds GPT-5.4 Mini to the Chat model picker.
- Chat requests for that model route to OpenAI's API with your own key.
- Added a guard so a configured provider's model cannot silently disappear from the picker again.

## Upgrade Notes

- No manual action is needed.
- If you already added an OpenAI key but its model did not appear, update the plugin, then refresh provider status or reconnect OpenAI.
- Minimum supported Obsidian version remains `1.4.0`.

## Fixes and Reliability

- Fixed OpenAI bring-your-own-key models not appearing in the Chat model dropdown after the provider was configured.
- Added a regression guard that checks every model offered in the picker has a working execution endpoint, so this class of dropdown gap is caught before release.

## Verification

Plugin checks, unit tests, and the built-bundle checks passed locally. The changes in this release also passed the macOS desktop baselines and the Windows clean-install and desktop-baselines end-to-end checks in continuous integration. Android and iOS device validation were not run for this patch.

# SystemSculpt 5.8.0

## What's New

SystemSculpt 5.8.0 adds image generation to the desktop Studio. A Studio image node turns a text prompt into images through SystemSculpt's hosted image service, with direct control over the model, aspect ratio, image size, seed, and how many images to generate per run.

This release also removes the legacy CanvasFlow feature, which decorated Obsidian's native canvas and was superseded by Studio.

## Highlights

- Generate images from a Studio image node: choose the model, aspect ratio, image size, seed, and batch count (up to 4).
- Leave the seed blank for random results, or set a whole number for reproducible output.
- The model picker only lists models that can actually generate images, so you never select one the service rejects.

## Upgrade Notes

- No manual action is needed.
- CanvasFlow has been removed; the desktop Studio view replaces it. Any saved `canvasFlowEnabled` setting is cleaned up automatically on upgrade.
- Image generation is a desktop-only Studio feature.
- Minimum supported Obsidian version remains `1.4.0`.

## Fixes and Reliability

- Image generation requests normalize cleanly: camelCase and snake_case option names are both accepted, and an image size the chosen model does not support is dropped instead of failing the request.
- Idempotent retries of an image job stay stable across the image-size change, so a repeated request replays the original job instead of returning a conflict.
- Selecting an unsupported image model now returns a clear invalid-model response.

## Verification

Plugin checks, unit tests, release surface checks, the macOS desktop baselines, the Windows clean-install and desktop-baselines GitHub check, and the Android sync + runtime smoke passed before release. iOS device validation was not run for this release.

## API and Platform Work Included

- Backend image-generation request schema hardening (camelCase option aliases, image-size-aware idempotency hashing, explicit invalid-model errors), deployed to api.systemsculpt.com ahead of this release.
- Removed the legacy CanvasFlow modules and relocated the shared image-generation modules to `src/services/images/`.

# SystemSculpt 5.7.1

## What's New

# SystemSculpt 5.6.0

## What's New

SystemSculpt 5.6.0 is a focused Search release. The in-vault Search modal now opens faster, keeps results steady while the content index catches up, and handles punctuated, multilingual, and symbol-only queries that used to drop out of results. Recent notes show up immediately for empty queries, and their snippets stay fresh after you edit a file.

If you use Obsidian's "Excluded files" filters, or you have embeddings enabled, this release also fixes several cases where Search used to disagree with your current settings until you reloaded.

## Highlights

- Search now opens with an instant recents list and starts returning metadata matches before the full content index finishes building, so the first results land almost immediately.
- Search now stays stable while the content index refreshes, so notes you are reading stop popping in and out of results between keystrokes.
- Search now finds punctuated queries like `orange-juice`, `don't`, and `co-op` against notes that contain the exact punctuated phrase, instead of silently dropping those hits after the index is ready.
- Search now handles multilingual and symbol-only queries more reliably, including CJK (e.g. `東京`), Cyrillic, and emoji-only terms.
- Recent notes now pick up fresh previews after an edit instead of showing a stale snippet until the next full search.
- Search now respects Obsidian's "Excluded files" filter the moment you change it, both for recents and for live search results.
- Smart mode now lazily starts the embeddings manager when embeddings are enabled, so users with auto-processing off still get semantic hits without a manual reload.

## Upgrade Notes

- No manual action is needed.
- Existing chats, settings, and search behavior should continue to work as before.
- Minimum supported Obsidian version remains `1.4.0`.

## Fixes and Reliability

- Fixed a case where changing Obsidian's "Excluded files" filter only took effect for the first change, leaving later edits ignored until an unrelated vault event.
- Fixed a case where starting a smart search during a background index build could leave excluded files searchable even after the filter had changed.
- Fixed short prefix queries (e.g. typing `fr` on the way to `fresh`) so they keep returning matches after the content index is ready.
- Fixed the empty-query recents list so it drops newly excluded notes and shows updated previews for recently modified files.
- Fixed a case where smart mode silently fell back to lexical-only when embeddings were enabled but the embeddings manager had not been initialized yet.

## Verification

Plugin checks, unit tests (5301 passing), and the release surface gate passed. CI `unit` and `desktop-baselines` checks are green on the merged PR.
